Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the GlobalBank Holdings Inc. third quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, during the Q&A session, please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. This event is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.  

Sarah Johnson:  
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review GlobalBank Holdings Inc.'s results for the third quarter. With me this morning are Johnathan Reeves, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Risk Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Credit Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer; Emily Carter, Chief Operating Officer; Tom Harris, Chief Marketing Officer; and Karen Lee, Chief Compliance Officer.  

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.  

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Reeves.  

Johnathan Reeves:  
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. GlobalBank Holdings Inc. delivered record results in the third quarter, exceeding all previous benchmarks and solidifying our position as a leader in the financial services industry.  

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on sustaining strong revenue growth, driving operational efficiency, managing risk effectively, investing in technology and innovation, enhancing customer experience, strengthening our brand reputation, promoting a diverse and inclusive culture, and delivering superior returns to our shareholders.  

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights. On technology investments, our substantial spending is transforming efficiency, reducing costs significantly and boosting scalability across operations. Regarding asset sensitivity, we're well-positioned with positive exposure to rate changes, supported by strong hedging strategies. Overall performance was outstanding, with record revenues and robust growth in both interest and fee income. Fee income saw impressive gains in wealth management, investment banking, and cards, driven by market recovery and client wins. Our deposit costs are managed tightly amid competition, maintaining favorable betas. Capital ratios like CET1 and Tier 1 are robust, exceeding requirements with room for returns. We're advancing capital returns through higher dividends and buybacks. Finally, our reserve dynamics reflect prudent releases tied to improving credit metrics and coverage.  

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.  

Michael Chen:  
Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning. GlobalBank Holdings Inc. reported net income of $9.2 billion for the third quarter, or $2.85 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.  

Net interest income increased 15%, driven by growth in our loan portfolio and improved net interest margin of 3.65%. Non-interest income was up 22% to $11.3 billion, reflecting strong performance in our investment banking and wealth management businesses. We are generating strong returns on equity of 18.2% and are committed to delivering value to our shareholders.  

Let me expand on these results, starting with our overall company performance highlights. We achieved record quarterly revenues of $32.4 billion, up 12% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter, powered by higher net interest income from elevated rates and robust fee growth. Adjusted net income hit $9.2 billion, beating consensus by 8%. This resilience shines through in segments: Consumer & Community Banking revenues grew 9% to $14.5 billion, with digital deposits up 20%; Commercial Banking up 13% to $8.2 billion; Investment Banking & Markets surged 25% to $7.9 billion; and Wealth & Investment Management up 11% to $6.5 billion. Regionally, U.S. operations grew 14%, Europe 8%, Asia-Pacific 18%. Credit quality is pristine, with net charge-offs at 28 basis points and provisions at $1.8 billion. Our technical initiatives, like cloud migration and GenAI fraud detection, are reducing costs and enabling innovation. Looking ahead, we target a 58% efficiency ratio and mid-teens ROE.  

Diving deeper into fee income, which totaled $2.8 billion, up 14% year-over-year, now 28% of total revenue. Wealth management led at $1.2 billion, up 18%, with AUM at $1.7 trillion from market gains and $45 billion in net new money. UHNW acquisition, Asia inflows, and our AI-powered WealthForge platform drove this, targeting 15-20% annual inflows. Investment banking fees hit $1.0 billion, up 12%, ranking us #4 in M&A, with $250 billion in deals advised, fueled by tech carve-outs and ECM rebound; our IB Nexus AI boosted hit rates. Cards fees reached $600 million, up 9%, on $450 billion volumes, with tokenization cutting fraud and co-branded partnerships adding accounts. We guide to $11-11.5 billion in full-year fees.  

On net interest income dynamics, our deposit franchise remains key. Average cost of deposits rose 18 basis points to 2.51%, with beta at 42%, moderated by 58% low-beta core deposits at 0.12%. Competitive pressures from Ally, SoFi, and money funds caused some outflows, but we grew deposits 1.2% to $154 billion ending. Dynamic pricing and Deposit Optimizer AI are retaining low-cost funds; we expect costs to peak soon, supporting NIM to 3.55%. Regionally, Midwest holds steady, West Coast faces more pressure.  

We're positively asset-sensitive, with +2.8% earnings at risk for a +100 bps shock, or $285 million NII uplift, and +4.1% over 24 months. EVE sensitivity is -3.2%, within appetite. Our $1.47 trillion assets have 62% repricing in 12 months, led by floating-rate loans; deposits beta at 42%. ALCO hedges via $180 billion derivatives and Murex ALM platform position us for +7-9% NII growth in 2024.  

Capital is strong: CET1 at 13.8% fully loaded Basel IV, up 40 bps, Tier 1 at 15.6%, 302 bps above our 10.8% G-SIB requirement. Numerator grew from earnings, denominator moderated by RWA optimization. Year-to-date organic capital exceeds targets, enabling returns. IRB recalibrations and securitizations shaved basis points; regionally robust across Europe, U.S., Asia.  

On capital returns, our Board approved a 10% dividend hike to $0.35 quarterly, payout at 42%. Q3 buybacks of $1.2 billion, YTD $3.8 billion. We plan $10-12 billion returns in 2024, 85-95% of earnings, balancing with growth.  

Finally, provisions saw a $175 million net release, reflecting lower recession risks, improved delinquencies at 1.12%, and charge-offs at 42 bps. CECL models with 300 variables drove releases in consumer and CRE, builds in international. ACL at 1.50% of loans, 285% of NPLs, exceeding peers. We guide flat-to-$100 million builds in H2.  

Our $1.2 billion tech spend, 9.5% of revenue, drove efficiency ratio to 57.2%, down 420 bps. Non-interest expenses fell 15%, cost per transaction to $0.14 with 92% STP. Cloud migration saved $180 million, Temenos platform enables open banking, AI fraud engine prevented $450 million losses, RPA $220 million savings. Regionally, digital mortgages in North America, RegTech in Europe, mobile in Asia. Tech-First model and venture arm position us for sub-55% efficiency next year.  

David Patel:  
Thank you, Michael. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring interest rate volatility, credit deterioration in CRE, geopolitical tensions, and cyber threats. We are implementing enhanced controls and monitoring to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile.  

Lisa Wong:  
Good morning. Our credit quality remains excellent with non-performing loans at 0.9% and criticized loans at 1.8%. We are actively managing our loan portfolio and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment.  

Raj Singh:  
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are leveraging technology to enhance customer experience, improve efficiency, and drive innovation. Our investments in AI/ML and cloud infrastructure are yielding significant results, aligning with the efficiency gains Michael outlined.  

Emily Carter:  
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include streamlining our processes, optimizing our infrastructure, and leveraging data analytics to improve decision-making, supporting our tech-driven savings.  

Tom Harris:  
Thank you. From a marketing perspective, we are focused on strengthening our brand reputation and enhancing customer engagement. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly successful in driving customer acquisition and retention, particularly in digital channels boosting wealth inflows.  

Karen Lee:  
Good morning. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of compliance and ethical conduct. We are continuously strengthening our compliance programs and working closely with regulators to ensure we are meeting all applicable requirements, including PSD2 and MiFID II.  

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.  

Operator:  
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.  

John Smith:  
Good morning. Could you please provide more detail on the outlook for net interest income given rate cut expectations?  

Johnathan Reeves:  
Good morning, John. We're well-positioned with our asset-sensitive profile and hedging, as Michael detailed. Even with anticipated Fed cuts, we project 7-9% NII growth next year through deposit innovations and selective floating-rate lending. Our low deposit beta and relationship focus will help stabilize margins.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.  

Maria Lopez:  
What is your outlook for fee income growth into next year?  

Michael Chen:  
Thanks, Maria. Fees are diversified and resilient, with wealth management leading on AUM expansion and UHNW wins, IB on M&A rebound, and cards on volume growth. We reaffirm $11-11.5 billion for FY24, with mid-teens potential in 2025 from embedded finance and cross-sell, despite macro risks.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.  

David Kim:  
Can you discuss the impact of CRE exposure on your risk profile?  

David Patel:  
Absolutely, David. Our CRE is well-managed at 4.2% of loans, with 85% performing and strong LTVs. Reserves cover criticized assets 320%, and we're de-risking office via restructurings. Stress tests confirm resilience, below peer averages.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with Barclays. Please go ahead.  

Alex Rivera:  
What are your plans for further technology investments?  

Raj Singh:  
Great question, Alex. Building on our $1.2 billion this year, we're guiding $1.4 billion next, targeting 300 bps more efficiency compression. Focus on GenAI scaling, blockchain for settlements, and fintech co-investments to capture embedded finance value.  

Operator:  
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Reeves for any closing remarks.  

Johnathan Reeves:  
Thank you for your interest in GlobalBank Holdings Inc. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.  

Operator:  
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
